title: Webflow Conf 2022 Brand System
content:
As Webflow ended 2022, we gathered our community — online and in-person — to celebrate the year and announce some exciting plans for the future. Here are the team’s thoughts as we built the visual system for the conference.

Co-Authored by: Rese Wynn, Jason Combs, Jessica Lopez, Patrick Szot

Visual Concept

Webflow gives you building blocks — and people use them with uninhibited imagination to experiment and break through barriers. By combining the visual language of transparency and the power of the the system, grid, and structure that does it all, we’re giving our community a chance to see right through us and go inside the interface and it’s many layers. Our visual system layers grids, gradients, our 2D and 3D “artifact” layer to play with depth and space in delightfully unexpected ways. We’ve created a unique visual playground that can move and flex to a maximalist brand in one moment, and a platform for the community in the next.

Grids, Gradients, Glitches

These are the the core ideas drive the visual concept of the system. Grids, padding indicators, and glitching containers serve as references to the underpinnings of building for the web. Gradients are used to illuminate those specific ideas or to color code aspects of the conference. We’ll optically turn up these core elements when the system is being more expressive, and turn them down when drawing the focus elsewhere.

Artifacts

Artifacts will mainly be used in the systems’ top Artifact layer. These artifacts, a combination of simple shapes and UI icons, are displayed in 2D and 3D. Artifacts are placed in a seemingly-unbounded, playful context. They are scattered across the top layer of our brand system to create unique moments of color, juxtaposition of ideas, or used in pools to reinforce themes or speaker topics. The artifacts should always feel as if they were randomly distributed across a layout. However, they should interact intentionally with the grid layer, if present. Artifacts can share sides or corners, but should not overlap each other.

Some shapes require optical sizing as such they will increase in size slightly to appear to be the same size as other artifacts.

All resizing of artifacts and grids should be done proportionately. Artifact default scale for digital applications is 25px but can be increased per the needs of the context. Some deliverable types will require sizing changes- these changes should be reflected in the artifacts size as well as the underlying grid. Glass panes and grids should, at their smallest, fit artifacts 1:2. Grid sizes can change, but should always be proportionate to the artifact size.

Artifacts are the smallest unit in the system. When the system’s scale is increased or decreased for specific executions, all elements should also be proportionately scaled.

Grid divisions can change but should always be proportionate to the base unit for the execution.

Artifacts have a separate palette, unrelated to the core brand palette.

Lighting and Color

The conference color palette gets its character from 4 core gradient swatches and the systems’ Artifact motif. Gradients serve as a connective tissue to the core Webflow brand and the conference brand. These gradient swatches are applied over fields of black and off-white.

The construction of brand gradients allows for organic, remixing of color that will flex depending on how layers are overlapped and move. Gradient swatches however, are limited in color as it pertains to a specific conference theme. Meaning graphics for the “build” portion of the conference should use the gradient and color palette designated for build. For graphics that span cross conference (Ex. Save the date) the gradients can be used flexibly.

Typography

While typography is not the hero of our system, we can use it flexibly to strike a balance between playful and serious. Graphik’s thinner weights are reserved and calming in our colorful brand system, but can shift on and off the grid to create moments of interest with headlines and speaker names.

Graphik is Webflow’s primary brand typeface, brought to new life through the use of the Webflow Conf brand system. Headlines in Graphik shift on horizontal and vertical axes, in and out of containers, on and off the grid.

Roboto Mono is a supporting typeface in the Webflow brand. It feels more digital and code-like, but just as Webflow isn’t a code-centric platform, Roboto Mono takes a backseat in the conference branding. It is only used for small details, captions, labels, and supporting text alongside Graphik.

Multiple weights and sizes of Graphik and Roboto Mono interplay to create typographic hierarchy.

1. Graphik headlines split and shift apart to create a central form with tight leading and tracking.
2. Roboto Mono is used small and in all caps for short details, and in sentence case for longer details or tertiary subheaders.
3. Graphik regular is used with -2% tracking and 150% line-height for body copy.

The mark designed for 2022 specifically will be used as the ‘logo’ in the majority of branded executions. This is a flexible type lock up that can be reorganized to fit different aspect ratios, sizes, and applications. Consider using this first as this the main logo for the conference and the company logo on the following page a supporting, more-formal logo.

Alternatively, the company-wide style Webflow Conf combination mark will be used year-over-year and as an alternate mark when talking about all things Webflow Conf.
